mission.title: open-policy-agent/opa: Add support for TLS certificate rotation in OPA's HTTP server
mission.description: OPA's HTTPS server loads the certificate given by --tls-cert-file only once at startup, so when the certificate file on disk is rotated (for example by cert-manager), OPA keeps serving the old, eventually expired certificate until the process is restarted. Upstream issue open-policy-agent/opa#2500 asked for a reload mechanism; OPA added the --tls-cert-refresh-period flag that polls the cert and key files and reloads them on change.

steps.title: Check current OPA deployment and version
steps.description:
Verify your OPA version and how it is deployed (the TLS certificate refresh flag requires OPA v0.39.0 or later):
```bash
kubectl get pods -n opa -l app=opa
kubectl exec -n opa deploy/opa -- opa version
helm list -n opa 2>/dev/null || echo "Not installed via Helm"
```
Adjust the namespace and label selector to match your installation.

steps.title: Confirm OPA serves TLS and identify the certificate files
steps.description:
Inspect the OPA server arguments to confirm it runs HTTPS with a static certificate:
```bash
kubectl get deploy opa -n opa -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].args}'
```
Look for `--tls-cert-file` and `--tls-private-key-file`. The symptom from open-policy-agent/opa#2500: if the files these flags point at change on disk (certificate rotation), OPA does not reload them — connections keep getting the certificate loaded at startup, which eventually expires.

steps.title: Add --tls-cert-refresh-period to the OPA server arguments
steps.description:
Enable periodic certificate reloading by adding the refresh flag to the OPA container args:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: opa
  namespace: opa
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: opa
        image: openpolicyagent/opa:latest
        args:
        - "run"
        - "--server"
        - "--addr=https://0.0.0.0:8443"
        - "--tls-cert-file=/certs/tls.crt"
        - "--tls-private-key-file=/certs/tls.key"
        - "--tls-cert-refresh-period=5m"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: certs
          mountPath: /certs
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: certs
        secret:
          secretName: opa-server-cert
```
With `--tls-cert-refresh-period=5m`, OPA re-reads the cert and key files every 5 minutes and swaps them in only when their content hash changes:
```bash
kubectl apply -f opa-deployment.yaml
kubectl rollout status deploy/opa -n opa
```

steps.title: Rotate the certificate and verify OPA picks it up without a restart
steps.description:
Trigger a rotation (with cert-manager: `kubectl delete secret opa-server-cert -n opa` forces reissuance, or renew via `cmctl renew`) and confirm the served certificate changes while the pod keeps running:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n opa -l app=opa -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.startTime}'
kubectl exec -n opa deploy/opa -- sh -c 'cat /certs/tls.crt | head -2'
echo | openssl s_client -connect $(kubectl get svc opa -n opa -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}'):8443 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -serial -enddate
```
The serial/notAfter reported by `openssl s_client` should match the new certificate within one refresh period, and the pod start time should be unchanged (no restart happened).

resolution.summary: The root cause is that OPA's HTTP server called tls.LoadX509KeyPair once at startup, so a certificate rotated on disk was never re-read and clients kept being served the stale certificate until the process restarted. Upstream resolved open-policy-agent/opa#2500 by adding the --tls-cert-refresh-period flag (OPA v0.39.0): the server polls the cert and key files on that interval, compares their content hashes, and atomically swaps the keypair via the tls.Config GetCertificate callback when they change. Setting the flag on the OPA container makes rotations by cert-manager or any file-based issuer take effect without a pod restart.
codeSnippets:
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: opa-server-cert
  namespace: opa
spec:
  secretName: opa-server-cert
  dnsNames:
  - opa.opa.svc
  - opa.opa.svc.cluster.local
  duration: 2160h
  renewBefore: 360h
  issuerRef:
    name: selfsigning-issuer
    kind: ClusterIssuer

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with open-policy-agent-opa- installed or the issue environment reproducible.
